common_name: Blue Triumphator Agapanthus (Tall Dark Violet-Blue Lily of the Nile)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun; a tall, statuesque agapanthus cultivar with dark violet-blue flower heads on sturdy scapes.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun. Blue Triumphator bears large, rounded flower heads in a rich, dark violet-blue on tall, strong scapes that stand well above the clump of narrow strap foliage, giving it good presence at the back of a mixed border or as a stately accent near a patio. Its height and deep color make it a useful contrast plant next to shorter, paler blue or white agapanthus cultivars. Like other agapanthus it is drought-tolerant once established and blooms best when slightly pot-bound, so avoid dividing established clumps too frequently.

common_name: Streamline Agapanthus (Compact Dwarf Blue Lily of the Nile)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun; a compact, heavy-blooming dwarf agapanthus popular for mass landscape planting.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun. Streamline produces medium blue flower heads in heavy abundance on a compact, dwarf plant considerably smaller than standard-sized agapanthus cultivars, making it a practical choice for mass planting along a walkway, edging a bed, or filling a smaller container. Its manageable size and reliable, floriferous performance have made it a popular commercial landscape selection. Like other agapanthus it is drought-tolerant once established and blooms best when slightly pot-bound, so avoid dividing established clumps too frequently.

common_name: Bressingham Blue Agapanthus (Classic Hardy Deep Blue Lily of the Nile)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun; a classic hardy deciduous-type agapanthus bred at the Bressingham gardens in England.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun. Bressingham Blue bears rounded heads of deep blue flowers on sturdy scapes above clumps of narrow, deciduous strap foliage, part of a long-established line of cold-hardy agapanthus cultivars developed at the famous Bressingham gardens that extend the plant's range well beyond the mild-winter climates most agapanthus cultivars require. Its deciduous habit, dying back to the crown in winter, gives it better cold tolerance than many evergreen agapanthus types. Like other agapanthus it is drought-tolerant once established and blooms best when slightly pot-bound, so avoid dividing established clumps too frequently.

common_name: Bressingham White Agapanthus (Classic Hardy White Lily of the Nile)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun; a classic hardy deciduous-type white agapanthus bred at the Bressingham gardens in England, a sibling to Bressingham Blue.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun. Bressingham White bears rounded heads of pure white flowers on sturdy scapes above clumps of narrow, deciduous strap foliage, sharing its cold-hardy, deciduous habit with its sibling Bressingham Blue, both developed at the famous Bressingham gardens to extend agapanthus growing well beyond the mild-winter climates most cultivars require. Its clean white color pairs easily with almost any other flower in a mixed border. Like other agapanthus it is drought-tolerant once established and blooms best when slightly pot-bound, so avoid dividing established clumps too frequently.

common_name: Crinum x powellii (Classic Pink Trumpet Hardy Crinum Lily)

planting.note: Plant large bulbs in spring in well-drained to moist, fertile soil in full sun to partial shade, with the neck of the bulb at or just above the soil surface; the classic pink-flowered garden hybrid crinum from which cultivars like the white-flowered 'Album' were selected.

directions: Plant large bulbs with the neck at or just above the soil surface in well-drained to moist, fertile soil in full sun to partial shade. Crinum x powellii is the classic garden hybrid crinum, a cross between Crinum bulbispermum and Crinum moorei that produces large clusters of fragrant, trumpet-shaped, soft pink flowers on tall, sturdy scapes above strap-like deciduous-to-evergreen foliage, and it is the parent from which several named color forms, including the white-flowered 'Album', have been selected. Once established, the massive bulb persists and multiplies for decades with essentially no care, making it a classic pass-along plant of old Southern gardens. It tolerates heat, humidity, and a range of soil conditions with ease, and division is rarely necessary, since crinum bulbs actually bloom best when left undisturbed and slightly crowded.
